summary: Intermittent 429s during canary/model-pin change on Dedicated VPC — cross-route token charging observed
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed spike of 429 throttles across multiple routes shortly after initiating a canary model pin change. Impact: intermittent request failures for production customers, increased error rates in low-latency endpoints, and invoice-impacting token accounting anomalies.

Impact: ~3% of requests returning 429 over a 12 minute window during deployment; customer reports app-level retries caused degraded user experience.

Environment: Dedicated pool in their VPC (reserved GPUs), edge gateway in front of private control plane, canary rollout toggled model pin from rw-infer-1.2-large -> rw-infer-1.3-quantized.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create two routes: /chat (low-latency, streaming) + /embed-bulk (batch). 2) Route both through the customer's internal gateway that rewrites headers for tenant routing. 3) Start steady traffic to /chat with multiplexed short-lived sessions and occasional large embedding jobs. 4) Trigger canary model pin flip for /chat to a new version while health-check autoscaler kicks warmups. 5) Observe intermittent 429 responses and throttle headers on both routes.

Observed headers (snippet):
- x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- x-rate-limit-reset: 23
- x-rate-limit-scope: tenant
- x-throttle-reason: route-accounting-mismatch

Customer asked: Are 429s expected during canary/model pin changes on Dedicated? How should we configure route isolation and warmup to avoid tenant-wide token exhaustion?
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ava Martinez (reporter): Filed after customer called support hotline — they attached a trace of 429 spikes and sample throttle headers.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Rohit Patel (assignee): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: warmup health-checks + model pin switch produced parallel warmup requests that were counted against tenant burst credits. Asking SRE to fetch per-route counters and gateway rewrite logs.

2026-03-10 10:08 - Customer (Pathway Analytics): We only see the issue for a few minutes during canary flips. We use a custom gateway that rewrites X-Route-ID headers for internal routing. We suspect the gateway might be replaying requests or duplicating connections.

2026-03-10 11:35 - SRE (Elena Wu): Pulled token accounting timelines from origin and edge. Noted a pattern where some warmup probe traffic shows up with two different route IDs within a 1s window, which would increment both per-route and tenant counters. Saving screenshots to Confluence page.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Rohit Patel: Test plan executed in staging with synthetic load and canary pin: reproduced 429 when gateway performed a header rewrite that caused route-id header to change mid-connection. Captured tcpdump and routing logs. Attaching links: https://internal-logs/pathway/trace/abc123

2026-03-12 14:05 - Rohit Patel: Mitigation applied to customer's gateway config to preserve X-Route-ID and route-affinity during model pin flips. Also adjusted dedicated pool warmup worker to use a low-priority weight so warmups draw from burst reserve last. Customer asked for follow-up and a permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Warmup probes and canary traffic were counted as separate routes due to header rewrite, causing double counting across per-route and tenant windows.
Hypothesis 2: Health-checks from autoscaler used short-lived ephemeral keys that were treated as independent token windows, draining tenant burst credits.

Test 1: Replayed canary flip in staging with packet capture. Result: gateway rewrote X-Route-ID for ~12% of sessions during pin change; origin received both old and new route ids and incremented both counters.
Test 2: Verified warmup worker priority weighting. Default weight was high; after lowering warmup weight, observed no tenant exhaustion under same synthetic load.

Findings: Primary contributor is the gateway rewrite behavior which changes route identity mid-flight; secondary contributor is warmup worker priority combined with short refill window. No evidence of duplicate request fanout at origin level (no duplicate request IDs in logs).
Related runbooks: Rate Accounting Runbook (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rate+Accounting+Runbook) used for troubleshooting and remedial steps.
resolution:
Applied immediate customer mitigation: updated gateway config to stop rewriting X-Route-ID during canary operations and set route-affinity TTL to 30s. Lowered warmup worker priority in the dedicated pool and enabled warmup rate limiting so warmups use the reserved burst bucket last.

Engineering fix planned: edge-router PR to add a header preservation flag during model pin rollouts (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/4123). Also added a console feature request to expose per-route token usage during deployments.

Customer impact mitigation notes: Customer restarted their gateway with patched config at 2026-03-12 13:50 and confirmed 0 throttles during a follow-up canary flip. Monitoring will continue for 72 hours.
follow_up_actions: Create RFC to formalize recommended warmup weight defaults for Dedicated pools (owner: infra-eng)
Edge-router: add header-preserve-during-rollout toggle and document in routing guide (owner: edge team, target: 2026-04-02)
Console: add per-route surge and token usage visualization during rollouts (owner: console team)
Document customer-facing KB: 'Avoiding tenant 429s during model rollouts in Dedicated VPC' (owner: docs)
Monitor Pathway Analytics tenant for 72h and follow up with customer on 2026-03-15
